subject: What can I do if the memory reach the limits when running scantwo?

messages.author: 49a67c6e0f03dace
messages.subject: What can I do if the memory reach the limits when running scantwo?
parts:
Hi Karl!

I recently want to run the scantwo, but it always appears the error "Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)" when it ran on chromosomes with huge amount of markers (I ran one chromosome at one time). Because of this problem, I can not run the permutation of the threshold for addpair function when performing multiple QTL mapping.

I googled this problem and some people say its the memory limits problem. They suggest to use 64 bit R. 

 I'm using 64 bit R and for chromosome with less marker, scantwo works without error. In this circumstance, what can I do with the chromosome with large amount of markers?

Could you please help me to solve this problem? 

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] What can I do if the memory reach the limits when running scantwo?
parts:
If you have a very large number of markers, you won't be able to run scantwo, because there will be too many pairwise interactions to test. So you'll need to switch to a different strategy.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] What can I do if the memory reach the limits when running scantwo?
parts: I sometimes reduce the number of markers in my map via findDupMarkers, pickMarkerSubset or reduce2grid. This will make scantwo more efficient.
